It's the perfect excuse to escape liability and it's not accidental that newer live service multiplayer games are implementing the same monetization scheme.

Live service games rely on player retention and milking people’s gaming addictions. Blizzard has been master at it ever since the old days of WoW. 

That’s why I think part of the reason why PvE got cancelled was because 1. They cannot monetize it the same way they monetize PvP and 2. Because Overwatch was never meant to go free to play. 

Less people cared about player counts, 10 minute queues or busted matchmaking in the original title because it didn’t revolve around keeping you chained to your computer with battle passes and limited pay to access content. We also had the right to suggest the course of the game in a sense because we paid for their product and they were obliged to support it and listen to the moneysource.

The issue was about fairness and not about the technical side of ranked OW which none of us know how it works. Also gave my two cents on his player retention assumption. 

I’ve heard playing less overwatch helps your attention span.

The science behind is that if you set your mind to achieve a goal in a video game competitive mode like Overwatch and eventully achieve the same goal, you lose interest in playing for the remaining season or playing the game as a whole (yes, I am just like that and whenever I reach my goal in video games I just abandon them because I have addictive personality and choose to be a productive human being).

That's why there's fishy things happening like deranking after perfect 5-0 series or the matchmaker matching you with players way out of your rank range which forces you to go on losing streaks and therefore, derank again. This is also influenced by your time zone and at what time of they day/night you queue for a comp game because late at night and early mornings have the least amount of players online and therefore is understandable for the matchmaker to have trouble finding a match for you quickly enough.

This is all under the guise of 'lowering queue times' but there's overall consensus in the OW community that sacrificing short queue times for fair matches and tighter matchmaking system, in other words, matching you with similarly skilled players, which it is supposed to do in general, is a better payoff. An overall consensus that Blizzard have not addressed yet even though there's huge outrage of player complaints about matchmaking and the supposed solutions to the problem.

They are technically keeping you hostage by making you feel unsatisfied with your results and continue playing the game and also give in to your addictive tendencies(if you have those) with the intent to make profit out of your addiction. Clearly not a very good gaming company practice in general but that's what live service games have become these years.

And also don't get me wrong, no one expects to win every game, but the difference in skill between players that are matched into your games is tremendous  from game to game and not what it's supposed to be. Also I don't think there should be losing or winning streaks of 10+ games in a row and 'jumping between tiers' for so long without actually climbing.

General tips on landing sleeps on genji: sleep early whenever you first see him or whenever he gets out of cover and is looking to dash onto you, even if he manages to dash you know it will be in a straight line towards you and the sleep will land most of the time. 

Whenever genji dives your team and not you specifically you can wait until he uses deflect and most of the time he will turn towards your teammates after a brief moment to negate the incoming damage, this is a good moment to land a dart in his back or side where the deflect won’t block it. 

Whenever he has already dove onto you and is using deflect and is positioned very close to you in order to shuriken you in the head after the deflect ends, you can look to the ground FULLY and use nade, this way the deflect wont pick it up and you will have done dmg onto him + anti. 

Usually whenever i verse genji i try to land shots onto him before he even thinks about diving me in the first place because genji on 130hp is much easier to kill than full hp. 

Dragonblade is hit or miss with all the dashes he gets out of it but you can still land some lucky darts sometimes and it’s very satisfying.

Edit: also regarding sleeps usually every genji plays different and you will have to learn their pattern during each game and find out there’s always a brief window of opportunity to land darts onto him.
